papers.title: RealityBench: Simulated Environments to Evaluate a Vision Language Model's Ability to Document Human Physical Work
papers.summary: Researchers benchmark vision-language models on simulated physical work tasks, finding strengths in text-based documentation but weaknesses in measurement reading, spatial reasoning, and acceptability judgment.

papers.title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models
papers.summary: RoboValue introduces a benchmark to evaluate robotic value models across task-state understanding, progress tracking, failure recovery, and consistency in both simulated and real-world settings.

papers.title: Harnessing Textual Refusal Directions for Multimodal Safety
papers.summary: MARS enables multimodal safety steering using only text-derived refusal directions, avoiding the need for multimodal safety data.

papers.title: Policy Is Not Capability: Some Safety Benchmarks Measure Which Definition of "Unsafe" You Trained On
papers.summary: Guardrail benchmark scores primarily reflect labeling policy rather than detection ability, with minor parameter changes shifting results across full ranges and training contamination undermining reported safety metrics.

papers.title: A Conditional No-Hair Theorem for Transformers: How Language Models Forget Their Prompt
papers.summary: Autoregressive transformers retain prompt influence via a power-law decay driven by attention dilution and relay mechanisms, with trained models forgetting faster than untrained ones.
